SoundWire.why: MIPI SoundWire is a real two-wire audio/peripheral bus; niche enough that Heisenbug fits.

1-Wire.why: Dallas/Maxim 1-Wire is a real peripheral bus. Known mainly to embedded and domain people, so Memory leak fits.

VMBus.why: Microsoft's Hyper-V virtual bus is a named system bus for virtual devices. Deep-internals knowledge, so Heisenbug fits.

SBus.why: Sun's SBus is a real expansion bus. Known to Sun and retro-hardware people, so Race condition fits.

MDIO.why: MDIO is the standard management interface between a MAC and an Ethernet PHY (IEEE 802.3 clause 22), a peripheral interface. Specialist knowledge, so Heisenbug fits.

AHB.why: AMBA AHB is ARM's real on-chip system bus. Embedded engineers know it, so Race condition fits.

STBus.why: STMicroelectronics STBus is a real on-chip interconnect bus. Deep-internals knowledge, so Heisenbug fits.

CardBus.why: CardBus is the 32-bit PC Card bus standard. Known to systems people, so Memory leak fits.

MII.why: MII is the IEEE 802.3 media-independent interface between a MAC and a PHY, a peripheral interface. Networking specialists know it, so Race condition fits.

SATA.why: Serial ATA is a real, very widely known storage/peripheral interface, so Off-by-one fits. 'SATA III' is a revision name, which is an acceptable alias.

SPI.why: Serial Peripheral Interface is a real, common embedded peripheral bus. Many hobbyists and engineers know it, so Null pointer exception fits.

Micro Channel.why: IBM's Micro Channel Architecture is a real expansion bus. It is known mainly to PC-history and systems people, so Memory leak fits better than Null pointer exception.

InfiniBand.why: InfiniBand is a real standard but a switched network fabric for servers and HPC, not a system, expansion or peripheral bus. It is neighbouring-domain networking, so it does not meet the category.

HyperTransport.why: HyperTransport is a real point-to-point system interconnect that replaced the front-side bus in AMD systems. Known to PC builders and enthusiasts, so Null pointer exception is plausible.

SAS.why: Serial Attached SCSI is a real storage/peripheral interface. IT and storage people know it, so Null pointer exception fits.

BCMA.why: BCMA is Broadcom's on-chip bus architecture, as used by the Linux bcma bus driver. Deep-internals knowledge, so Heisenbug fits. Membership is from memory of the kernel driver, not a source line I could check here.

AVSBus.why: I cannot confirm this is a real, named bus standard. It may be a voltage-scaling control interface, but the strict rule says to reject when unsure it exists.

Multibus.why: Intel's Multibus (I and II) is a real, historically significant system bus. Only specialists know it, so Heisenbug fits.

LPC.why: Low Pin Count is Intel's real bus that replaced ISA on PC motherboards. Firmware and PC specialists know it, so Race condition fits.

DIO.why: DIO is HP's real Direct I/O expansion bus on its 9000 series 200/300 workstations. Deep-internals knowledge, so Heisenbug fits.
